objectives: Segment taught bl-words into phonemes before spelling.
Represent both /b/ and /l/ in the correct order at the start of each word.
Spell taught words such as blob, blip, blot, black and block accurately.
Reread each spelling to check the vowel and ending.
concepts: Encoding moves from heard phonemes to graphemes in the same order.
A blend keeps both consonant sounds; spelling must represent both letters b and l.
The rime determines the rest of the spelling, including ck where taught.
Read-back is a self-check, not just a speed exercise.

definitions.definition: Represent spoken sounds with written graphemes.
Separate a spoken word into its phonemes in order.
A letter or letter group used to represent a phoneme.
Read a written word after spelling it to check that it matches the intended word.

workedExamples.solution: Map /b/ /l/ /a/ /k/ to b-l-a-ck, using ck for the final /k/ in this taught word.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct “bak” when the target is black.
workedExamples.solution: Add the missing l after b and represent the final /k/ with ck: black.

commonMistakes: Leaving out l and writing back for black.
Writing the letter names instead of mapping each sound.
Using k instead of the taught ck pattern in black or block.
Not reading the completed word to check it.

Read the word back and correct any missing grapheme.

conceptual.prompt: Why must l be written after b in black?
conceptual.answer: Because /l/ is the second phoneme in the initial blend.

conceptual.prompt: What should you do before spelling a word?
conceptual.answer: Segment the full word into phonemes in order.

conceptual.prompt: Why read the word back after spelling it?
conceptual.answer: To check that every sound and grapheme matches the target.

application.prompt: Correct “bak” when the target word is black.
Spell the word with onset bl and rime -ip.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How do you decide between blob and blot when spelling?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Listen to the final phoneme: /b/ in blob or /t/ in blot.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: What is wrong with writing black as b-l-a-k?
higherOrderThinking.answer: The taught spelling uses ck for the final /k/.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How can sound boxes help with bl?
higherOrderThinking.answer: They keep the phonemes in order and help prevent leaving out /l/.

mixedReview.prompt: Which word ends with ck: blot or block?

mixedReview.answer: Read the word back and check each sound.
